newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Dec 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Dec 24.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company

-- SFA WORRIED BY LARGE BONUSES The head of the Securities & Futures Authority, Richard Farrant, has joined other regulators in expressing fears that big City bonuses could encourage excessive risk taking and make firms more vulnerable to a downturn. His comments come amid reports of record bonuses for top staff of City firms.

-- BT AND BSKYB PAY-TV LINK IN THE AIR The telecoms regulator, Oftel, is believed to be poised to give the go-ahead to BSkyB and British Telecom in a digital television joint venture. The plans would see both companies take an equity stake along with other commercial partners. Oftel has asked for further details of how open the proposed technological platform would be, and is expected to insist that the new venture be kept distant from BT and BSkyB's main businesses.

-- BAA EYES ST PANCRAS FOR SECOND HEATHROW RAIL LINK BAA, the airports operator, is seeking approval to run a second service between Heathrow and central London, having already secured a high-speed service between Paddington and Heathrow, due to start in June 1998. The second service will be slower and run between St Pancras, the planned fast rail link with the Channel tunnel, and Heathrow, with four stops en route.

-- NORTHERN'S FATE TO BE DECIDED TODAY The Takeover Panel held an emergency meeting last night to consider Northern Electric's plea for independence. The panel met to rule on Northern's request to overturn an extension to the bid period which will give control to CE Electric. The outcome of CE Electric's bid depends on whether the Takeover Panel's executive overturns a decision made on Friday to extend the bid period to lunchtime today. CE Electric had captured only 49.77 per cent of shares by Friday lunchtime, the original deadline, but late acceptances had pushed it to victory with 50.33 per cent.

-- SEARS ON BRINK OF FREEMANS DEAL Sears revealed yesterday that it is close to agreeing the sale of its Freemans home shopping business to Littlewoods for between 350 and 400 million pounds stg. Littlewoods had to overcome other bidders thought to include Otto Versand of Germany, N Brown and Great Universal Stores. The Office of Fair Trading will have to indicate that it does not intend to refer the bid to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission.

-- RJB PLANS TO LIFT EARNINGS WITH 34 MILLION POUNDS SHARE BUYBACK The independent coal producer, RJB Mining, has announced plans for a 34 million pounds stg share buyback. RJB, whose shares fell 23 per cent earlier this month after its broker, BZW downgraded its profits forecasts for the next two years, said the company wanted the ability to lift earnings per share through a buyback while the share price was subdued.

-- MOBILE SWAP EASES BG'S BURDEN British Gas have announced agreed terms with Mobil to swap North Sea assets for more competitive supply terms. British Gas claim that the move will unscramble nearly a fifth of its burden of financially crippling long term gas contracts. British Gas will hand over a 5 per cent interest in the Beryl gas field, a near 30 per cent stake in a block in the Nevis field and 2.5 per cent in the Scottish Area Gas Evacuation system, to clinch the deal with Mobil.

-- FINANCE CHIEF GRANT LEAVES LUCASVARITY LucasVarity, the Anglo-American engineering group was surprised yesterday by the resignation of its finance director John Grant. The resignation is likely to be taken by the City as proof that the former Varity directors may be taking precedence over the ex- Lucas board. Mr Grant will be replaced by Neil Arnold, who was Varity's chief financial officer before the merger of Lucas and Varity earlier this year.

-- MCDONALD'S WISES UP TO THE POOR TASTE OF WILTED LETTUCE McDonald's, the fast food corporation, that has 18,300 outlets in 101 countries, is having problems selling burgers in its US home. It is being forced to change its recipe after its own research showed that people prefer burgers at rivals Wendy's and Burger King.

-- INTEREST RATES MAY RISE AS HOUSING MARKET FIRMS The possibility of another interest rate rise before the general election was strengthened yesterday by minutes of Octobers monthly meeting between the Chancellor, Kenneth Clarke, and Eddie George, governor of the Bank of England. The governor said that the quarter point increase implemented on 30 October, might well not be enough to moderate the upswing sufficiently to restore a better than even chance of achieving the inflation target over the next two years.

-- DEUTSCHE BANK LOSES TOP RATING Deutsche Bank suffered another embarrassment yesterday when it was demoted from the elite club of triple-A rated banks. The move by Moody's, the New York credit rating agency, comes in the wake of the Morgan Grenfell Asset Management scandal and means that only a handful of banks are still ranked in the financial world's premier league of credtiworthiness.

-- SHARES ROW CLOUDS NORWICH FLOTATION Norwich Union's planned flotation on the stockmarket was thrown into controversy yesterday as it was revealed that many thousands of members in line for a free shares bonanza may have been fraudulently recruited. Norwich Union said it had yet to take disciplinary action against any of its staff for encouraging the sale and back-dating of insurance policies.
